props.description: The people, in the order they stack (the first on the inline-start side).
props.name: items

props.description: How many avatars show before a "+N" count stands for the rest. Defaults to 4.
props.name: max

props.description: The group's accessible name, for example "Assigned staff".
props.name: label

props.description: The background behind the fallback: neutral or the tone's soft colour. Defaults to `default`.
props.name: variant

props.description: The diameter and the text size of the initials. Defaults to `md`.
props.name: size

props.description: The colour role of the initials and fallback icon. Defaults to `default`.
props.name: tone

props.description: A circle for people, a rounded square for organisations. Defaults to `circle`.
props.name: shape

props.description:
How stacked avatars overlap visually.
- `"clip"` — crescent mask (transparent seam; no box-shadow)
- `"ring"` — solid box-shadow outline via `--background`
Has no effect when `isGrid` is true.
props.name: overlap

props.description:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.
props.name: render

props.description:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
props.name: ref
